examples.label: Base64-encode the PHP webshell for the payload

notes: Unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2018-7600) covering Drupal 7 and 8 - the highest-value option when the version matches. The base64 step just smuggles the PHP shell past request parsing.
name: Drupalgeddon2 - RCE (CVE-2018-7600)
description: Exploits CVE-2018-7600 (Drupal 7/8) for unauthenticated RCE, typically dropping a base64-decoded PHP webshell that is then invoked with a command parameter.

defense.why_it_works: Drupalgeddon2 (CVE-2018-7600) exploits the Drupal Form API. User-supplied '#' prefixed form properties are processed by AJAX callbacks without sanitization, injecting arbitrary PHP callbacks that execute system commands. No authentication required.
defense.prerequisites: Drupal 7.x < 7.58 or 8.x < 8.3.9/8.4.6/8.5.1. Unauthenticated -- the vulnerable endpoint is accessible without login.
defense.impact: Unauthenticated RCE as www-data. Webshell placement. Full server compromise from a single HTTP request.
defense.detection: POST request to /user/register or Drupal forms with '#' prefixed parameters. IDS signature for CVE-2018-7600 payload pattern.
defense.artifacts: Web server access log (POST to /user/register with exploit payload) | IDS alert for Drupalgeddon2 signature | New .php file created by web server process
defense.prevention: Update to Drupal 7.58 / 8.5.1 or later immediately. Enable automated security update notifications. Apply WAF rules with CVE-2018-7600 signatures.
defense.misconfiguration: Unpatched Drupal 7.x or 8.x accessible from the internet without WAF protection.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Drupal 7.x < 7.58 or 8.x < 8.5.1
# Vulnerable form element handling in form.inc
# '#post_render', '#type' callbacks not sanitized
defense.secure_config:
# Patch to current Drupal release
drush pm-update
# WAF rule: block '#' prefixed parameter names in POST bodies
defense.evasion: URL-encode payload to bypass simple WAF string matching. Use multipart form encoding.
